os_version: 24.04.5 LTS (Noble Numbat) with a 64-bit (x86_64) kernel and userland, used to run 32-bit i686 executables through the i386 multiarch libraries; NOT a native 32-bit system
environment_detail: NOT A NATIVE i686 SYSTEM. This record describes the 32-bit (i686, gcc -m32) build of the Linux Legacy UI as it was built and run on the machine of validation/platforms/linux-ubuntu-24.04-x86_64.json: the same WSL2 distribution Ubuntu-24.04 with WSLg on the same Windows 11 host, with the same 64-bit Microsoft WSL2 kernel 6.18.58.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 (uname -m x86_64) and a 64-bit userland. The 32-bit executable runs on that 64-bit kernel in compatibility mode, on the x86_64 CPU of the host, through the Debian multiarch architecture i386 (dpkg --print-foreign-architectures: i386): gcc-multilib 4:13.2.0-7ubuntu1 and the i386 packages libc6 2.39-0ubuntu8.12, libx11-6 2:1.8.7-1ubuntu0.1 and libx11-dev, and, installed by the owner on 2026-11-14 for the Xft text path, libxft2 and libxft-dev 2.3.6-1build1 and libfontconfig1 and libfontconfig-dev 2.15.0-1.1ubuntu2 (measured with dpkg-query on 2026-11-14). Before that installation the machine had no 32-bit libXft, so the i686 build took the core-font fallback xlib-core-font-glyphs; since then it finds Xft. It talks to the XWayland server of WSLg like the x86_64 build. What this record does NOT represent: a 32-bit Linux kernel, a 32-bit-only distribution (such as an i386 Debian or an old Ubuntu), an i686 CPU without x86_64 (no 32-bit-only processor was used), a real old machine, or any system older than Ubuntu 24.04. The spec (Clarifications, architectures) asks for x86 32-bit and x64 on Linux, and the Linux Legacy UI is built on the machine that runs it (ADR 0007); the i686 build is therefore recorded as a platform of its own in scope, but with a verdict still to be written, and the only thing measured for it is that this build links and runs under multiarch on the machine above (validation/deliverables/linux-i686-legacy.json). Its probe lines report the id of the host platform (linux-ubuntu-24.04-x86_64), not linux-i686, because the application derives the id from /etc/os-release and uname.
eol_source: Same kernel and distribution as linux-ubuntu-24.04-x86_64: the backend (loomora_is_eol) does not treat kernel 6.18 on Linux as end of life, and eol_warning_shown is false in the stored probe line of the i686 build (validation/evidence/linux-build-on-target/linux-ubuntu-24.04-x86_64/xlib-core-font-fallback-i686-probe-mixed.txt).
kernel: 6.18.58.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 (uname -srm: Linux 6.18.58.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64), a 64-bit vendor kernel: the 32-bit program runs in compatibility mode
glibc: 2.39 (libc6:i386 2.39-0ubuntu8.12 for the 32-bit program; the 64-bit libc6 of the distribution is the same release)
compiler: gcc 13.3.0 with -m32 (cmake/toolchains/linux-gcc-i686.cmake, gcc-multilib 4:13.2.0-7ubuntu1), cmake 3.31.12 (see the deliverable record)
hardware: The host of windows-11-x64: MSI GL63 8RD, Intel Core i5-8300H (a 64-bit CPU, used here in x86_64 long mode with the kernel running 32-bit programs), 8 logical CPUs and 20003 MB visible in the WSL2 VM; not an i686-only machine
release_date_source: Same as linux-ubuntu-24.04-x86_64 (distro-info-data: release 2024-04-25 for 24.04 LTS); age_years = days from that date to 2026-11-14 divided by 365.25 = 2.55.
